Q10.his_words: Q10: Draft order is correct … always the class broker sends.
Q10.what_was_built: He approved the draft order. NOT BUILT, and for a reason he should see: the draft I wrote puts the institution's own class field first, which is the opposite of his own brief B7 (2026-08-20), "name first, broker tag as fallback only". That brief came from his Vanguard money-market fund being counted as cash because the tag overrode the name. “always the class broker sends.” For a linked or imported holding, the class the broker sends decides what it is. The name, a maturity date and the app's other automatic rules are used only when the broker sends no usable class. A class the person sets themselves still outranks every automatic rule. Example: a money-market fund the broker flags as cash is Cash; a T-bill ETF the broker sends as an ETF is Stocks / Funds.

Q11.his_words: Q11: Refuse the line and ask
Q11.what_was_built: When nothing says what a holding is, the app does not guess. The holding is counted in no class — it shows as Unclassified — and Net worth asks the person what it is. Their answer ends the asking and stays through every sync.

Q12.his_words: Q12: user entry stays even if it is not in the import file. If user modify cost or quantity post import/linked from institution, cost basis should not be overwritten in future sync as quantity, price and market value can change with time but not cost.
Q12.what_was_built: What a person enters on a linked account stays. A holding they added stays even when the broker's list does not carry it. A cost they set is kept by every later sync: the shares, the price and the value follow the broker, the cost per share does not.

Q14.what_was_built: An account is called by its name. No class word is printed under it — not "Mixed", not "Unclassified".

Q04.his_words: perfect. Commit it all, and execute PFS.
Q04.what_was_built: Every change from the fifth batch of the outside review of Net worth stands as his decision: a face value or rate never entered is blank, never $0; one rule for a year of interest; a matured bond pays nothing more; yields use the price without accrued interest; the rates-move estimate compares like with like and refuses a CD; years count calendar days; a confirmed account is never re-classed; a record with no accounts is nothing saved.

Q05.his_words: I like your recommendation to add accrued interest. Say "Added estimated $1,119 in accrued interest to bond value at 4.5% coupon for 363 days to calculate YTM. If this is not accurate, enter actual accrued interest"
Q05.what_was_built: The value typed for a bond is what the statement shows, which leaves out the interest earned since the last coupon. For the yield to maturity, that interest is added: the figure entered, or an estimate from the coupon schedule, and then the screen reads: "Added estimated $1,119 in accrued interest to bond value at 4.5% coupon for 363 days to calculate YTM. If this is not accurate, enter actual accrued interest". The yield on today's value is on the value as entered. A $25,000 4.5% Treasury worth $24,200 two days before its coupon now reads 5.69%, not 7.44%.

Q37.his_words: 4 - why the app does not block user from selling more than what's in portfolio. … then: "3,4, 8-approved."
Q37.what_was_built: A linked broker sends about two years of activity, so a sale can reach past the oldest purchase it sent. Example: bought 10 at $50 on record, sold 15 at $70. The sale is counted once; its gain is on the 10 matched shares; the page reads "$200 gain on 10 of 15 shares sold; what you paid for the other 5 is not on record." Before, it counted one sale with a gain AND one sale without a purchase, which read as two sales. A sale typed by hand is still blocked from selling more than you own.
